baseProblem.statement: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.

rounds.question: Which property of this problem makes a sliding window the right tool?
options: The answer is always a contiguous substring with a constraint that can be checked incrementally
The problem has a fixed window size known in advance
rounds.explanation: Sliding window fits when the answer is contiguous and the validity check (no duplicates here) can be maintained as the window grows or shrinks.

rounds.question: When the right pointer sees a character that's already in the window, what should the left pointer do?
options: Reset all the way back to the start
Jump to the position just past the previous occurrence of that character
Stay put until the right pointer moves past the duplicate
rounds.explanation: Jumping straight past the previous occurrence skips invalid windows in one step. Moving one at a time also works but is slower in the worst case.

rounds.question: What's the time complexity when using a hash map to track character positions?
rounds.explanation: Each character is visited at most twice — once by the right pointer, once by the left. Total work is O(n).

rounds.question: The hash map stores the last index seen for each character. When you find a duplicate, can the left pointer ever move backwards based on the map?
options: Yes — the map says jump to position 5, so set left = 5 regardless of where it was
No — the left pointer should only move forward; take max(left, mapIndex + 1)
Yes — but only if the duplicate is more than k positions away
It doesn't matter — the answer comes out the same either way
rounds.explanation: If you don't clamp with max, a duplicate from outside the current window can drag the left pointer backwards and invalidate the count. Classic off-by-one bug.

rounds.question: Which input is most likely to expose the bug from Round 4?
rounds.explanation: When right reaches the second 'a', the map says position 0 — but left is already at 2 after handling the 'b'. Without max-clamping, left drags backwards.
